Remark. The Mittag-Leffler residue sum as a heuristic shadow of the Habiro expansion

Remark (what the Mittag-Leffler picture actually was). The earlier "\sum_{n,j} r_n^{(j)}/(q_0 - \zeta_n^{(j)})" expression is a formal residue spectral sum (GB residue spectral sum) — a heuristic shadow of the Habiro expansion valid only after one fixes a finite cyclotomic order and a regular evaluation point q_0 disjoint from S^1. It is not a convergent sum on or near S^1 and does not define \mathrm{tr}_M as a meromorphic function on \mathbb{C}. Each finite-order Cauchy-kernel partial sum is the q-adic image of a Habiro truncation; computational data confirms that for the proton and neutron the Cauchy kernel partial sum truncated at n \leq 6 is identically zero, in agreement with property (2) of the mass-trace pole structure (prop:full-pole-structure-mass-trace) (the Habiro coefficients a_0, \ldots, a_5 vanish on the atomic trefoil class).
